$comment: Cases for the delivery-cadence rule (design §6). A prober implementation exposes a pure function over this input and must produce this output. The rule exists because the extranets hibernate and every delivery wakes one: a healthy tenant costs one wake an hour, a tenant with something down is woken every cycle, which is the cost you want to pay.

input.now: the moment the cadence is being evaluated
input.last_delivery_at: when this tenant last had a successful delivery, or null if never
input.previous_status: the monitor's status before the latest result: up, down, or null when this is its first ever result
input.latest_status: the status of the newest buffered result
input.buffered_count: how many undelivered results are held for this tenant

reasons.down: the latest result is a failure; deliver now and on every cycle it stays down
reasons.recovery: the monitor went from down to up; deliver once more immediately
reasons.cadence-elapsed: everything is up, but the batch interval has passed
reasons.first-delivery: nothing has ever been delivered for this tenant; deliver so the link is proven
reasons.buffered-while-up: everything is up and the batch interval has not passed; hold

cases.name: first result of all, monitor up
cases.note: A fresh prober delivers once rather than waiting an hour, so an unreachable extranet is discovered at boot instead of 60 minutes later.

cases.name: up, batch interval exactly elapsed
cases.note: The boundary is inclusive; 60 minutes after the last delivery is due, not one cycle later.

cases.name: up, batch interval elapsed, nothing buffered
cases.note: The cadence does not manufacture an empty delivery. Reachability is proven by the manifest reconcile pull instead.

cases.name: first failure
cases.note: The first failed check wakes the extranet. The extranet's own consecutive-failure threshold decides whether anyone is paged; the prober does not.

cases.name: still down on the next cycle
settled again after a recovery
cases.note: Recovery delivers once. The cycle after it is an ordinary up result and goes back to being batched.

cases.name: down under a per-tenant cadence override
cases.note: The cadence override changes only the batch interval. Nothing shortens or lengthens the immediate delivery of a failure.
